evidence: I read the CONTEXT section cold, then the draft inside it, the last sentence of the section's final paragraph: "Used together properly, the subconscious can feel safer in giving its response, though that doesn't make the answers any more true." It follows from the two sentences before it (the prompt tells the subconscious what you want; the NLP in Appendix B "can help smooth the prompt's entry and reduce resistance"): less resistance, so the subconscious can feel safer, and the caveat then limits what that safety proves. "Used together" means the prompt and the NLP, as in his original; that opener is a loose participle in form, but it is his, unchanged, and the two sentences before it make it plain. Pronouns: "that" is the subconscious feeling safer (the same referent his "That" had, now adjacent; the other possible reading, using the two together, gives the same caution); "its" is the subconscious's; "the answers" are the answers it gives, as in his text. Against SOURCE.txt I compared word by word: every word is kept; the full stop becomes a comma, "That" becomes "that", and the closing "though" moves to the front of the clause. Nothing is added or dropped, and the meaning is kept: feeling safer does not make the answers any truer. There is one shift of weight only: the caveat was a standalone sentence and is now the last clause of one sentence. It still closes the sentence and the section, and the cautions earlier in the section ("checked it against what I actually know") carry the same point, so it is not buried. It matches the_change exactly: DRAFT.txt equals the quoted joined sentence and CONTEXT.txt holds it once. Tells: I judged every row T01 to T29 and C01 to C04 against the literal sentence in its paragraph and found none actually PRESENT. Near misses I checked: T17 and T12 (the safer / not-more-true pair is a caution that the section's other cautions earn, it was already in his two sentences, and it is specific to the answers these prompts give, not a packaged aphorism; the join does not turn it into a thesis line); T18 (the shape of a premise followed by a short flip is what the join removes, and what is left qualifies the premise rather than reversing it); T20, T28 and T29 (the last sentence adds a new consideration, ends on a caution, and is neither a restatement, a clever closer nor uplift); T21 (two points joined by subordination, one qualifying the other, not a list of coordinated jobs); T11 and T07 ("though" is his own word doing the concession, not a bridge or filler); T15 (no word swapped); T26 ("true" recurs from "true guidance" in the third prompt, as a thematic callback, not a repeated phrase); C02 and C04 (no wrong or forward referent, no named entity in the draft). Linter: "D9 follows the source order" is accepted. This is an in-place join of his two sentences, so the order of points stays the same by design, and the caveat is the thing the sentence notices (T13), with no equalized weight (T09). I took the Pangram results in the_change as stated; I could not verify them (no web). I judged from the three files first and opened ADMISSION.json afterwards; my rows agree with the writer's.
